author: cbaelectronicos
quote:
Creative Abilities: Ultrahand lets players glue objects and Zonai devices into custom vehicles and contraptions, while Fuse combines weapons, shields, and arrows with items for varied combat effects. Ascend and Recall add vertical traversal and time-reversal problem-solving.
Expanded Vertical World: Seamless transitions connect a revamped Hyrule surface with floating Sky Islands and the dark, subterranean Depths.
Player Freedom & Dungeons: Open-ended puzzles, over 150 shrines, themed temples, and boss fights reward experimentation and creative solutions. As IGN notes in its review, the new mechanics and multi-layered map elevate the Breath of the Wild formula into a massive, cohesive adventure.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition

author: cbaelectronicos
quote: widely praise its unrestricted open-world freedom, physics-driven mechanics, and reinvention of Zelda conventions, while noting minor drawbacks like weapon durability and occasional frame rate drops

author: cbaelectronicos
quote: I'm not going to say the game is completely broken, but it's close. I encountered several problems in the first 18 hours of gameplay. While not completely broken, it's definitely broken. There are already videos online showing bugs and glitches everywhere, but perhaps that's not the worst part. There are also things that aren't broken but are poorly thought out, designed, and executed. The physics of characters, NPCs, and vehicles are poor and basic. Sometimes people look like crash test dummies; their movements don't seem realistic and they feel heavier than they should be. The gameplay is very clunky, heavy, and lacks fluidity and agility. The sound effects are average, nothing impressive. The music? It doesn't have any original music. There aren't any memorable original tracks that you'll find yourself humming in 10 or 20 years. Everything is licensed from other artists. This aspect is very weak; not creating original music and relying on the budget to pay for licenses is a very, very bad point. And the performance? You can't be so hypocritical. Either performance deducts points from all games, or it doesn't deduct points from any. Games like Starfield were killed for their performance at launch. There's no dubbing. It's one thing for games in the '80s or '90s not to have dubbing, but in 2026, most games have dubbing in multiple languages: Spanish (ES, LA), Portuguese (PT, BR). The AI ​​isn't well-balanced. I found several situations where the NPCs' behavior in relation to Jason didn't make sense. As for fun, the story mode, if you only follow the story mode, is more than boring, it's incredibly boring. Innovation? There's no innovation in anything, folks, nothing. Not in gameplay, physics, music, or sound effects. Graphically, they're not innovations, just improvements on GTA V and RDR2. But come on, how can a game that doesn't innovate in any aspect have a 99? Even the menu isn't innovative, and on top of that, it's quite shoddy, basic, and ugly, in short. The Woke story of me teaming up with Jason to do everything Lucia wants could be the best game of 2026, but far from being the best in history, it will possibly remain the most overrated game of all time.
